sermon-t03-02.model_answer: The central message of 'The Sermon at Benares' is that death is universal and that attachment to the dead causes suffering. Kisa Gotami initially believes that her dead son can be restored to life. Buddha helps her understand reality through the simple task of collecting mustard seeds from a household untouched by death. Her search shows her that every family has faced loss. She gradually understands that no human being can escape death. The lesson encourages acceptance rather than endless grief. It also suggests that wisdom comes from understanding the natural cycle of life and death.

Her teacher has already taught her to value herself and speak without fear. Bholi therefore refuses to accept a marriage based on humiliation and greed. supp-necklace-d02.model_answer: The necklace is ironic because Matilda believes it represents wealth and social status, but it ultimately causes years of poverty. She borrows it to appear elegant at the ball and believes that it is valuable. After losing it, she and her husband replace it by borrowing a large amount of money. They spend ten years working hard and living in difficult conditions to repay the debt. Matilda's entire life changes because of the necklace. At the end, she learns that the original necklace was only an imitation. The irony lies in the fact that an object she thought was extremely valuable was actually worth very little.
